experiences.name: Praia Dona Ana Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, just a short walk from Lagos town center. Praia Dona Ana features dramatic golden limestone cliffs, crystal-clear turquoise waters, and soft sand. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella, explore the sea caves by foot at low tide, and enjoy fresh seafood at the beachside restaurant.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a local Lagos wine bar near the historic center, sampling regional Algarve wines including Vida Nova rosé and Quinta dos Vales reds, paired with local cheeses and charcuterie. Learn about the unique terroir of the Algarve wine region from a knowledgeable sommelier.

experiences.name: Ponta da Piedade Kayak & Snorkel Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic sea caves and golden rock arches of Ponta da Piedade on a guided kayak tour departing from Lagos marina. Snorkel in hidden grottos and lagoons teeming with marine life, and witness breathtaking coastal scenery accessible only by water. A perfect blend of adventure and natural beauty.

experiences.name: Quinta dos Vales Vineyard Tour & Tasting
experiences.description: Take a half-day excursion to one of the Algarve's premier wineries, Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, followed by a tasting of five award-winning wines including their signature Marquês dos Vales Grande Reserva. The estate also features impressive outdoor sculptures and stunning countryside views.

experiences.name: Meia Praia Sunset Beach Walk & Seafood Dinner
experiences.description: Stroll along the vast 4km stretch of Meia Praia, a wide sandy beach just east of Lagos, during the golden hour for spectacular Atlantic sunset views. Afterward, dine at a local beachside restaurant serving freshly grilled fish, cataplana seafood stew, and local Algarve wines, combining the best of beach culture and regional cuisine.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €5-7, ~1.5 hours). Check into Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack from a nearby convenience store or a slice of pizza from a late-night spot near the hostel. Budget: €3-5

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Faro to Lagos bus ticket online to save time. The hostel is centrally located in Lagos, making it easy to walk to most attractions. Keep luggage light for the bus journey.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hostel or a nearby pastelaria. Stroll through Lagos old town, explore the historic city walls, and visit the free Igreja de Santa Maria church in the main square (Praça Gil Eanes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Meia Praia Beach (about 2 km from the hostel or a short bus ride). This long, wide sandy beach is perfect for swimming and relaxing. It's less crowded than the famous grottos beaches and completely free to access.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Lagos town center. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril for budget dining options. Enjoy a sunset stroll along the marina.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mulher de Capote near the town center — coffee and pastel de nata for €2-3
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local Mercado de Lagos (fresh bread, cheese, fruit) for €4-6
meals.dinner: O Camilo or a local tasca on Rua 25 de Abril — prato do dia (dish of the day) with soup, main, and drink for €8-10

day_by_day.notes: September is still warm and sunny in the Algarve (avg 25°C), perfect beach weather. Bring sunscreen and a reusable water bottle to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Ponta da Piedade — a stunning coastal rock formation just 2 km south of Lagos. Walk or rent a bike (€8-10/day from local shops near the hostel). Explore the clifftop trails and viewpoints for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the steps to the sea caves and grottos at Ponta da Piedade. Hire a local fisherman's boat tour of the grottos (€10-15 per person, negotiate directly with the boat operators at the bottom of the steps for the best price). Visit Praia do Camilo nearby — a small, beautiful beach accessible via wooden steps.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Visit the Mercado de Escravos (Slave Market Museum) — entry is around €3 — one of the oldest slave markets in Europe, a sobering but important historical site.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast if included, or grab a galão (milky coffee) and tosta mista (toasted sandwich) at a local café for €3
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Ponta da Piedade or bring packed snacks — bifanas (pork sandwiches) from a local café for €2-3
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina near the marina — grilled fish or cataplana for €10-12

day_by_day.notes: Go to Ponta da Piedade early morning to avoid crowds and get the best light for photos. The boat tours are cash only, so bring small bills.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus (EVA Bus, €2-3) to Sagres, the southwestern tip of Portugal. Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) — a historic fortress with stunning Atlantic Ocean views and wind rose.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Cabo de São Vicente (about 6 km from Sagres or take a taxi for €8-10 shared) — the most southwestern point of continental Europe. The lighthouse and cliffs are breathtaking. Explore the small market stalls selling local crafts and dried fish.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Relax at the hostel and socialize with fellow travelers in the common area.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hostel or a café near the bus station — €3-4
meals.lunch: A Sagres restaurant near the fortress — fresh grilled sardines or tuna steak for €9-11
meals.dinner: Self-catering from Pingo Doce supermarket in Lagos — pasta, local cheese, wine for €5-7 total

day_by_day.notes: Buses from Lagos to Sagres run several times daily. Check the EVA Bus schedule in advance. Sagres can be windy even in September, so bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take a bus or rideshare to Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (approx. 30 km east of Lagos). Book a budget wine tasting session in advance (€10-15 per person for 4-5 wines). The Algarve produces excellent local wines including Negra Mole and Crato Branco varieties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue wine exploration at Quinta da Penina or visit the Lagos Wine Cellar (Adega Cooperativa do Algarve) closer to town for a more affordable tasting (€5-8). Purchase a bottle of local wine to enjoy later.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Stroll along the marina at sunset with your purchased wine. Visit the free viewpoint at Forte da Ponta da Bandeira for golden hour views.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha in Lagos town center — coffee and croissant for €2-3
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery if offered, or a nearby café — €8-10
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Vivant in Lagos — affordable Portuguese tapas and wine for €12-15

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead to confirm winery opening hours and tasting availability. Some wineries require reservations. Consider sharing a taxi with hostel mates to split costs.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Albufeira (1 hour by bus, €5-6 each way). Visit the old town and the famous Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) — a beautiful beach right in the town center, free to access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Albufeira's sea caves and cliffs. Walk the clifftop path to Praia de São Rafael (about 3 km west) — one of the most scenic beaches in the Algarve with dramatic rock formations. Swim and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Albufeira's old town streets and the lively Rua Cândido dos Reis. Head back to Lagos by evening bus.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or Lagos café before departure — €3
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia dos Pescadores — grilled chicken piri-piri wrap for €6-8
meals.dinner: Back in Lagos — Tasca do Zé or similar local tasca — bacalhau (salt cod) dish for €9-11

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira can be touristy and pricier than Lagos. Stick to local tascas away from the main strip for better value. The bus journey offers scenic Algarve countryside views.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia da Luz, a charming village beach 6 km west of Lagos. Take the local bus (€1.50) or walk along the coastal path. The beach is wide, calm, and less crowded than Lagos beaches. Swim and explore the black rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk back toward Lagos along the scenic coastal cliffs (about 1.5 hours). Stop at Praia do Porto de Mós — a beautiful, quieter beach with golden cliffs. Relax and swim.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Lagos, visit the weekly local market if it falls on this day, or browse the artisan shops on Rua da Barroca. Enjoy a sundowner at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local padaria (bakery) — fresh bread and coffee for €2-3
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia da Luz — fresh fish sandwich and local beer for €7-9
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Dois Irmãos in Lagos — seafood rice or grilled sea bass for €11-13

day_by_day.notes: The coastal walk from Praia da Luz to Lagos is stunning but can be warm. Start early and bring plenty of water. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve (30 min by train from Lagos, €3-4 each way). Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry) with panoramic views over the orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves Cathedral (Sé de Silves, free entry) and the charming old town streets. Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia (€2 entry). Walk along the Arade River banks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the hostel common area. Try some of the local wine purchased earlier in the trip.

meals.breakfast: Quick café stop before catching the train — galão and pastel de nata for €2-3
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for affordable grilled chicken and local specialties, €10-12
meals.dinner: Self-catering at the hostel — local cheese, presunto (cured ham), olives, and bread from the supermarket for €5-6

day_by_day.notes: The train from Lagos to Silves is scenic and very affordable. Check the CP (Comboios de Portugal) schedule. Silves is quieter and more authentic than coastal towns — a great contrast.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Dona Ana — one of Lagos's most photographed beaches, just 1.5 km from the hostel. Arrive early to secure a good spot. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water surrounded by golden limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the clifftop trail from Praia de Dona Ana toward Ponta da Piedade (already visited on Day 3, but the trail itself is worth doing in full). Stop at hidden coves and viewpoints along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Ponta da Piedade viewpoint. Return to Lagos for dinner. Visit the lively Rua 25 de Abril for evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hostel — scrambled eggs on toast and coffee for €4-5
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia de Dona Ana — fresh orange juice and a sandwich for €5-6
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Galeão in Lagos — traditional Portuguese pork or fish dishes for €10-12

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Dona Ana has limited shade, so bring an umbrella or arrive early. The clifftop trail can be uneven in places — wear sturdy sandals or trainers.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — visit Herdade do Esporão or a local Algarve wine cooperative. Alternatively, join a free or low-cost wine and food pairing workshop sometimes offered at local wine shops in Lagos town center. Ask at the hostel for current recommendations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lagos Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal) for fresh local produce, cheeses, and regional products. Pick up affordable souvenirs like local honey, fig jam, or medronho (arbutus berry spirit). Explore the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a communal dinner at the hostel kitchen using market ingredients — a great way to save money and meet fellow travelers. Make a simple cataplana-inspired dish with clams, tomatoes, and local wine.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen — toast, local jam, and coffee for €2
meals.lunch: Market snacks — olives, local cheese, fresh bread for €4-5
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hostel meal — ingredients from the market for €6-8 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos Municipal Market is best visited in the morning when produce is freshest. Cooking at the hostel is a great budget strategy and a fun social activity.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha (20 min by bus from Lagos, €2-3). Praia da Rocha is one of the Algarve's most famous beaches — a long stretch of golden sand with dramatic orange rock formations. Arrive early to enjoy it before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Portimão town center. Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sunday afternoons, €3 other times) — an excellent museum in a converted sardine canning factory. Walk along the Arade River waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Try Portimão's famous grilled sardines at one of the riverside restaurants — a local specialty and very affordable. Return to Lagos by bus.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagos before departure — €3
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia da Rocha — fresh fruit and a bifana for €5-6
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Portimão — grilled sardines, bread, and local wine for €9-11

day_by_day.notes: Portimão is famous for its sardine festival (usually in August, but the tradition continues). The grilled sardines here are considered among the best in Portugal — don't miss them!

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final relaxed morning at your favorite Lagos beach — Praia de Dona Ana, Meia Praia, or Praia do Camilo. Take a long swim and soak up the last of the Algarve sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore any remaining Lagos sights — the Forte da Ponta da Bandeira (€3 entry, a 17th-century fort at the marina entrance), or revisit the old town for last-minute souvenir shopping. Visit the local artisan market if available.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos. Splurge slightly on a nicer meal to celebrate the trip. Visit a local wine bar for a final Algarve wine tasting — try a glass of local Moscatel dessert wine.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or similar — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, toast, and coffee for €5-6
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach snack bar — grilled fish and salad for €9-10
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina or similar — splurge on a cataplana (traditional Algarve seafood stew) for €15-18, shared between two

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do any last-minute shopping, pack, and prepare for departure. Check bus/train times to Faro Airport for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Boutique Taghostel. Store luggage at the hostel if needed for a few hours. Take a final morning walk through Lagos old town — visit the Igreja de Santo António (€3 entry, stunning gilded baroque interior) if not visited earlier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Faro Airport via EVA Bus or Rede Expressos from Lagos bus station (€5-7, ~1.5 hours). Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for the journey and check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the Algarve's beaches, wines, and culture.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and coffee at a Lagos café — €2-3
meals.lunch: Snack at Faro Airport or pack leftovers from the hostel — €5-8
meals.dinner: On the flight or at the destination

day_by_day.notes: Keep your bus ticket receipt in case of any issues. The Lagos to Faro bus is reliable but book in advance during peak season. Leave a review for the hostel — it helps other budget travelers!

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

Praia Dona Ana features dramatic golden limestone cliffs, crystal-clear turquoise waters, and soft sand. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella, explore the sea caves by foot at low tide, and enjoy fresh seafood at the beachside restaurant.

Learn about the unique terroir of the Algarve wine region from a knowledgeable sommelier.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the airport shuttle or a pre-booked taxi (~1 hour, ~€50–60) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour convenience store or the hostel's common area if snacks are available.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from a convenience store near the hostel or airport café before departure

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – arrival is late. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid waiting. Confirm check-in arrangements with Taghostel as arrival is after 22:00. Pack a small snack in your carry-on for the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café. Take a gentle orientation walk around Lagos old town – explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia Dona Ana Beach (a 15-minute walk from the hostel) for your first taste of the Algarve's stunning coastline. Relax on the golden sands, swim in the crystal-clear Atlantic waters, and admire the dramatic ochre limestone cliffs. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella (~€10–12) for a comfortable afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll back into Lagos town center for dinner. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril restaurant strip. After dinner, enjoy a casual drink at one of the outdoor bars along the marina waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a local pastelaria near the hostel – try a pastel de nata and galão coffee (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Light snack or sandwich from a beach kiosk at Praia Dona Ana (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant near Praia Dona Ana or Restaurante Adega da Marina on the waterfront – fresh grilled fish or cataplana (~€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: September is an excellent time to visit – crowds thin out after August but the sea is still warm (~22°C). Apply sunscreen generously even in September. The walk to Praia Dona Ana is scenic and easy from the hostel.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Ponta da Piedade Kayak & Snorkel Tour (book in advance, departs ~09:00–09:30 from the beach below Ponta da Piedade, ~10-minute taxi or walk from hostel). Paddle through the iconic golden sea caves, arches, and grottos of one of the Algarve's most spectacular coastal landmarks. The guided tour typically lasts 2.5–3 hours (~€35–45 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, dry off and have lunch in Lagos. Spend the early afternoon exploring the Mercado de Lagos (municipal market) for fresh local produce, cheeses, and cured meats. Browse the artisan shops along Rua da Barroca for handmade ceramics and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Join the Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting Experience at a local Lagos wine bar near the historic center (book in advance, typically runs ~19:00–21:00, ~€30–40 per person). Sample regional Alentejo and Algarve wines paired with local cheeses and charcuterie – a perfect introduction to Portuguese wine culture.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or Pastelaria Mota on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva – coffee and toast with local jam (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Tasca do Celso in Lagos old town – petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and a glass of local wine (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Wine and cheese provided during the tasting experience; supplement with a light post-tasting snack at a nearby tapas bar if still hungry (~€8–10)

day_by_day.notes: Book both the kayak tour and wine tasting well in advance as September still sees good tourist numbers. Wear quick-dry clothing and water shoes for the kayak tour. Bring a waterproof bag for your phone and valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or taxi (~30 minutes, ~€15 by taxi or €3.50 by bus) to Sagres, the dramatic southwestern tip of Portugal. Visit the imposing Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry), a 15th-century fortress perched on a windswept promontory with breathtaking Atlantic views. Explore the giant wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos) and learn about Portugal's Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or taxi to Praia do Beliche or Praia de Sagres for a more rugged, wild beach experience compared to Lagos. These beaches are less crowded and backed by dramatic cliffs. Alternatively, hike the coastal path from Sagres toward Cabo de São Vicente (the southwestern-most point of continental Europe, ~6 km round trip) for spectacular scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus or taxi. Have dinner in the old town and enjoy the Friday evening atmosphere with live music often playing in the squares and bars.

meals.breakfast: Café Central in Lagos before departure – fresh orange juice, toast, and eggs (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: A Sagres – Restaurant Bossa Nova or a local café in Sagres village – grilled sardines or tuna steak (~€14–18)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nah Nah Bah in Lagos – burgers and craft beer in a relaxed setting, popular with locals and travelers (~€14–18)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September – bring a light jacket. The last bus back to Lagos typically departs around 18:30–19:00; check the Eva Transportes schedule. Cabo de São Vicente is a must-see for sunset if timing allows.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle from a Lagos bike shop (~€12–15/day) and cycle along the coastal path toward Meia Praia, a long sweeping beach stretching east of Lagos. The flat cycle path is easy and scenic, passing the marina and estuary. Arrive at Meia Praia (~20-minute ride) for a morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue cycling or relax at Meia Praia. In the mid-afternoon, cycle back to Lagos and visit the Museu de Lagos (Lagos Municipal Museum, ~€3) housed in a former church – fascinating exhibits on the region's history, archaeology, and the Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.evening: Saturday evening in Lagos is lively. Head to the Rua Soeiro da Costa bar street for pre-dinner drinks, then enjoy a leisurely dinner at one of the town's best restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Meu Limão café in Lagos – avocado toast, smoothie bowl, or açaí (~€8–12) – a popular healthy breakfast spot
meals.lunch: : Beach kiosk or snack bar at Meia Praia – prego sandwich (steak roll) and a cold beer (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos old town – traditional Portuguese cuisine, excellent bacalhau (salt cod) dishes (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday markets sometimes appear near the Lagos waterfront – check locally. Meia Praia is popular with kitesurfers and windsurfers, making for great people-watching. Return bikes before the shop closes (usually 18:00–19:00).

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Silves, the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve (~45 minutes by train from Lagos, ~€3.50 each way – the train station is a short walk from the hostel). Visit the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry), one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal, with panoramic views over orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves town – visit the Gothic Sé Catedral de Silves (free entry), stroll along the Arade River promenade, and browse the Sunday market if running. Silves is surrounded by citrus and almond orchards – the landscape is distinctly different from the coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Enjoy a relaxed Sunday evening dinner and an early night to recharge.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastry and coffee at Lagos train station café before departure (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves – a charming restaurant inside the castle walls serving traditional Algarvian dishes (~€14–20)
meals.dinner: Tasca da Praça in Lagos – a cozy local tasca with daily specials, excellent value (~€12–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check the train timetable in advance – Sunday services may be less frequent. The train journey itself is scenic, passing through the Algarve countryside. Silves is quieter than Lagos and offers a wonderful contrast to the beach scene.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day at Praia Dona Ana – your second visit to this stunning beach, this time with more confidence about the best spots. Arrive early (~09:00) to secure a prime location before day-trippers arrive. Swim, snorkel with your own mask and snorkel (rentable nearby), or simply relax and read.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the clifftop path from Praia Dona Ana toward Praia do Camilo (15-minute walk) – a smaller, more secluded beach tucked between towering cliffs, accessible via a wooden staircase. Spend the afternoon here for a quieter experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a wine-focused evening. Visit a local wine shop such as Garrafeira do Mercado to pick up a bottle of Alentejo red or Vinho Verde, then enjoy it with a charcuterie board at a rooftop bar or the hostel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or a local padaria (bakery) – fresh bread, cheese, and ham (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach – pick up supplies from a local supermarket (Pingo Doce on Rua Portas de Portugal) – bread, local cheese, olives, fruit, and cold cuts (~€8–10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco – small, intimate restaurant with excellent petiscos and regional wines (~€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The clifftop walk between Praia Dona Ana and Praia do Camilo is one of the most scenic short walks in the Algarve. Wear sturdy sandals or shoes as the path can be uneven. Praia do Camilo has a small beach bar for refreshments.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha (~30 minutes by bus from Lagos, ~€3.50). Praia da Rocha is a wide, dramatic beach backed by a clifftop promenade. Walk the promenade, explore the 16th-century Fortaleza de Santa Catarina (free entry) at the eastern end, and enjoy the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Portimão town center (10-minute bus ride from Praia da Rocha). Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays, ~€3 other days) – an award-winning museum in a converted sardine canning factory telling the story of the Algarve's fishing heritage. Browse the riverside market stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Before returning to Lagos, have dinner in Portimão – the town is famous for its grilled sardines. Return to Lagos by bus in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Café near the Lagos bus station before departure – coffee and croissant (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Rocha – fresh seafood sandwich or grilled fish (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré in Portimão – renowned for charcoal-grilled sardines and local seafood, excellent value (~€14–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Portimão hosts the Formula 1 Portuguese Grand Prix at the Algarve International Circuit nearby – check if any motorsport events are scheduled during your visit. The bus between Lagos and Portimão runs frequently throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wine exploration day. In the morning, visit the Lagos Wine House or a local adega (winery) for a morning tasting session focusing on Algarve DOC wines – the region produces excellent reds from Negra Mole and Castelão grapes. Many wine bars open from 10:00 for tastings (~€15–20 for a guided flight).
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a car for the afternoon (~€35–45/day from a local agency) or join a guided tour to visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (~40 minutes east of Lagos). This acclaimed estate offers vineyard tours and tastings with stunning sculpture gardens (~€15–25 per person for tour and tasting). Book in advance.
day_by_day.evening: Return the rental car and enjoy a relaxed evening in Lagos. Visit the Mercado de Escravos (Slave Market Museum, free or small donation) before it closes, then have a wine-paired dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mota near the hostel – fresh pastries and coffee (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery restaurant or a nearby café in Estômbar – local bread, cheese, and wine (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos – excellent wine list with traditional Algarvian cuisine, try the cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales is one of the Algarve's most photogenic wineries with impressive outdoor sculptures. If driving after wine tastings, designate a non-drinking driver or arrange a taxi. The Algarve wine region is less famous than Alentejo but produces excellent, underrated wines.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat trip from Lagos Marina – choose a half-day coastal cruise along the Ponta da Piedade coastline (~€25–35 per person, departs ~10:00). These boat tours enter sea caves inaccessible by kayak and provide a different perspective of the golden cliffs. Many tours include snorkeling stops.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the boat trip, have lunch near the marina. Spend the afternoon visiting the Igreja de Santo António (Church of St. Anthony, ~€2) – a stunning 18th-century baroque church covered in gilded woodwork, considered one of Portugal's finest baroque interiors. Adjacent is the Museu Regional de Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class or food experience – check if any local operators offer Portuguese cooking classes in Lagos (typically €45–65 per person, 2–3 hours). Learn to make cataplana or pastéis de nata. Alternatively, enjoy a sunset cocktail at a clifftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Meu Limão or a marina café – smoothie and eggs before the boat trip (~€8–10)
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Galeão near the marina – fresh grilled sea bass or dorado (~€16–22)
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner (if booked) or Restaurante Bica in Lagos – intimate restaurant with excellent daily fish specials (~€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat trip at least a day in advance – multiple operators depart from Lagos Marina. September seas are generally calm, making for excellent boat conditions. The Igreja de Santo António is a hidden gem that many visitors overlook.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the western Algarve's wild coast – take a taxi or rental car to Praia do Amado (~45 minutes north of Sagres). This stunning, remote beach is a world-class surf spot. Take a beginner surf lesson (~€35–45 for 2 hours including board and wetsuit) or simply watch the surfers while enjoying the wild, unspoiled scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or taxi through the Costa Vicentina Natural Park – stop at Carrapateira village for lunch, then explore the dramatic Bordeira Beach (Praia da Bordeira), a vast wild beach with a river estuary and sand dunes. Walk the wooden boardwalk through the dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for your final full Friday evening. Celebrate with a special dinner at one of Lagos's top restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel or a Lagos café before departure (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Sitio do Rio in Carrapateira – a beloved local restaurant with fresh fish and stunning views over Bordeira Beach (~€16–22)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vasco da Gama in Lagos – upscale but mid-range, excellent wine list and creative Portuguese cuisine (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Costa Vicentina is one of Europe's last unspoiled Atlantic coastlines – part of the Parque Natural do Sudoeste Alentejano e Costa Vicentina. Bring a windbreaker as the exposed beaches can be breezy. This area has minimal tourist infrastructure so bring cash.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning – return to your favorite beach (Praia Dona Ana or Praia do Camilo) for a last swim in the Atlantic. Take your time to soak in the scenery, collect a few pebbles or shells as mementos, and enjoy the September sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping in Lagos old town – pick up local products: Algarve olive oil, local wines (look for Vida Nova or Quinta dos Vales bottles), handmade ceramics, cork products, and almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo is the traditional Algarve sweet). Visit the Saturday market near the waterfront if running.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner with a special wine pairing – choose a restaurant with an excellent Alentejo and Algarve wine list. Reflect on the trip over a long, leisurely Portuguese dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha – a proper sit-down breakfast with fresh orange juice, eggs, and local bread (~€8–10)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach café or snack bar – keep it simple for the last beach day (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião – your farewell dinner, splurge slightly on a tasting menu or the chef's special with wine pairing (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pack your purchases carefully – wine bottles need bubble wrap or wine travel bags (available at most wine shops). Check your luggage weight allowance. Confirm your airport transfer for the following day if departing on Day 13.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos – wake up early for one last pastel de nata and galão at a local café. Take a slow walk along the Lagos city walls and down to the marina for a final view of the Algarve coastline. Check out of Boutique Taghostel (standard checkout is 11:00 – arrange luggage storage if needed).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, either relax in a café in the old town or take a taxi to Faro Airport (~1 hour, ~€50–60). If time allows, explore Faro's charming old town (Cidade Velha) near the airport – the walled historic center, Faro Cathedral, and the unusual Bone Chapel (Igreja dos Ossos) are all within walking distance of the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Carry a bottle of local Algarve wine in your checked luggage as a delicious reminder of your trip.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and coffee at a Lagos pastelaria – savor every bite (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Airport café or a quick bite in Faro old town if time permits (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Faro Airport. The airport is small but can get busy on Sunday afternoons. Pre-book your transfer to avoid last-minute stress. Portugal's VAT refund (Tax Free Shopping) is available for non-EU residents – collect your forms from shops and process at the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia Dona Ana Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, just a short walk from Lagos town center. Praia Dona Ana features dramatic golden limestone cliffs, crystal-clear turquoise waters, and soft sand. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella, explore the sea caves by foot at low tide, and enjoy fresh seafood at the beachside restaurant.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a local Lagos wine bar near the historic center, sampling regional Algarve wines including Vida Nova rosé and Quinta dos Vales reds, paired with local cheeses and charcuterie. Learn about the unique terroir of the Algarve wine region from a knowledgeable sommelier.

experiences.name: Ponta da Piedade Kayak & Snorkel Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic sea caves and golden rock arches of Ponta da Piedade on a guided kayak tour departing from Lagos marina. Snorkel in hidden grottos and lagoons teeming with marine life, and witness breathtaking coastal scenery accessible only by water. A perfect blend of adventure and natural beauty.

experiences.name: Quinta dos Vales Vineyard Tour & Tasting
experiences.description: Take a half-day excursion to one of the Algarve's premier wineries, Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, followed by a tasting of five award-winning wines including their signature Marquês dos Vales Grande Reserva. The estate also features impressive outdoor sculptures and stunning countryside views.

experiences.name: Meia Praia Sunset Beach Walk & Seafood Dinner
experiences.description: Stroll along the vast 4km stretch of Meia Praia, a wide sandy beach just east of Lagos, during the golden hour for spectacular Atlantic sunset views. Afterward, dine at a local beachside restaurant serving freshly grilled fish, cataplana seafood stew, and local Algarve wines, combining the best of beach culture and regional cuisine.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) whisks you to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (~55 min). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of local Algarve wine left by the hotel.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night charcuterie and cheese board arranged by the hotel upon arrival, paired with a glass of Vinho Verde

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with Boutique Taghostel. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority after a long-haul flight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a premium breakfast at the hotel. Explore Lagos old town on foot — stroll through the historic Praça Gil Eanes, visit the Igreja de Santo António, and wander the charming cobblestone streets to get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia Dona Ana Beach Day — one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches, just a 15-minute walk from the hotel. Settle into a premium sun lounger, swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters, and explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs and sea caves along the shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up, then enjoy a sunset aperitivo on the hotel terrace. Dinner at Dom Sebastião Restaurant in Lagos — a Lagos institution renowned for its exceptional fresh seafood, grilled fish, and regional Algarvian cuisine in an elegant setting.

meals.breakfast: Full premium breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — fresh pastries, local cheeses, cured meats, fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach-side café near Praia Dona Ana — grilled sea bass, fresh salads, and chilled local white wine
meals.dinner: Dom Sebastião Restaurant, Lagos — try the cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) or grilled turbot with regional wines

day_by_day.notes: Praia Dona Ana is a short walk from the hotel — no transport needed. Book dinner at Dom Sebastião in advance as it fills quickly in September.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, join the Ponta da Piedade Kayak & Snorkel Tour — a guided paddle through the world-famous sea caves, golden rock arches, and hidden grottos of Ponta da Piedade. The morning light on the cliffs is spectacular. Snorkel in the clear Atlantic waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos and enjoy a leisurely lunch. Spend the afternoon exploring the Mercado de Lagos (local market) and browsing boutique shops in the historic center. Visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) for cultural depth.
day_by_day.evening: Join the Algarve Wine & Cheese Tasting Experience at a curated Lagos wine bar near the historic center. Sample regional Alentejo and Algarve wines paired with artisan Portuguese cheeses, cured meats, and local preserves, guided by a knowledgeable sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh fruit, yogurt, local honey, pastéis de nata, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: A Forja Restaurant, Lagos — beloved local spot for traditional Portuguese grills and fresh fish in a rustic-chic setting
meals.dinner: Wine and cheese tasting experience serves as a gourmet evening — supplement with a light post-tasting supper at Casinha do Petisco tapas bar

day_by_day.notes: Book the kayak tour in advance — morning slots fill fast in September. Wear reef-safe sunscreen and bring a change of clothes for after the kayak tour.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow morning breakfast at the hotel. Take a private taxi or hire a driver for a half-day excursion to Quinta dos Vales Vineyard near Estômbar (~35 min from Lagos). Arrive for the Quinta dos Vales Vineyard Tour & Tasting — explore the estate's vineyards, wine cellar, and sculpture garden, then enjoy a guided tasting of their premium reserve wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos after the vineyard tour. Spend a relaxed afternoon at leisure — perhaps a spa treatment at a nearby luxury wellness center or a quiet afternoon reading by the hotel pool or terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Villas Alvor Boutique Hotel's restaurant or the acclaimed Bon Bon Restaurant (Michelin-starred, Carvoeiro, ~25 min) for an extraordinary fine-dining experience showcasing modern Algarvian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with fresh-squeezed orange juice, local pastries, and cold cuts
meals.lunch: Vineyard lunch at Quinta dos Vales — a curated wine-paired lunch on the estate terrace featuring regional produce (book in advance)
meals.dinner: Bon Bon Restaurant, Carvoeiro — Michelin-starred tasting menu with wine pairing (reservation essential, book weeks ahead)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private driver for the vineyard excursion so you can enjoy the wine tasting without worrying about driving. Book Bon Bon well in advance — it is one of the Algarve's most sought-after tables.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take a private boat charter from Lagos Marina for a morning cruise along the stunning Algarve coastline — passing sea caves, hidden beaches, and dramatic cliffs. Many luxury charters include snorkeling stops and onboard refreshments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark and head to Meia Praia — the vast 4km sandy beach east of Lagos. Settle in for a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathe on this quieter, more expansive beach. Rent premium sun loungers and enjoy the wide open Atlantic views.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Meia Praia Sunset Beach Walk & Seafood Dinner — stroll along the golden sands as the sun dips below the horizon, then sit down to a spectacular fresh seafood dinner at a beachside restaurant, with the sound of the waves as your backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs your way, smoked salmon, fresh fruit platters, and artisan bread
meals.lunch: Light onboard snacks and chilled rosé wine during the boat charter, or a quick bite at Lagos Marina
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at Meia Praia — grilled whole sea bream, tiger prawns, and percebes (barnacles) with chilled Alvarinho white wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter at least 2–3 days in advance. September weather is typically warm and calm — ideal for coastal cruising. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light layer for the evening beach walk.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely hotel breakfast followed by a private guided cultural walking tour of Lagos — delve into the city's Age of Discovery history, Moorish heritage, and maritime legacy with an expert local guide. Visit the city walls, the Golden Chapel, and the old fishing quarter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive (~45 min) to the dramatic Cape St. Vincent (Cabo de São Vicente) — the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Explore the windswept cliffs, the historic lighthouse, and the fortress. The views are breathtaking and the light in the afternoon is extraordinary.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a relaxed evening. Enjoy pre-dinner cocktails at a rooftop bar in Lagos, then dine at Restaurante Adega da Marina — a premium waterfront restaurant known for its exceptional cataplana dishes and extensive Portuguese wine list.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with local specialties
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch at Cape St. Vincent — arrange a luxury picnic basket through the hotel with local cheeses, charcuterie, bread, and wine
meals.dinner: Adega da Marina, Lagos — cataplana de lingueirão (razor clam stew) or grilled monkfish with regional wines

day_by_day.notes: Cape St. Vincent can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The sunset from the cape is legendary but the drive back in the dark is straightforward. Arrange the gourmet picnic basket with the hotel the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — enjoy a long, indulgent hotel breakfast and a slow start. Book a luxury spa morning at a nearby wellness center or arrange an in-room massage through the hotel. Alternatively, take a gentle yoga session on the hotel terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Praia do Camilo — a smaller, more secluded beach near Ponta da Piedade, accessible via a wooden staircase through the cliffs. Swim in the sheltered cove and enjoy the dramatic rock formations. Bring a good book and simply unwind.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private sunset wine tasting on a clifftop terrace — arrange through a local luxury concierge service for an intimate experience with a sommelier, featuring Alentejo reds and Algarve whites paired with local tapas as the sun sets over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — take your time with fresh pastries, local honey, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near Praia do Camilo — fresh salads, grilled sardines, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant, Lagos — perched dramatically above the cliffs near Praia do Camilo, serving exceptional fresh fish and seafood with panoramic ocean views

day_by_day.notes: O Camilo is one of Lagos's most scenic restaurants — book a window table well in advance. The clifftop sunset tasting can be arranged through the hotel concierge or a local luxury experience provider.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, take a private day trip east along the Algarve coast to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) and the Gothic Cathedral with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the charming hilltop village of Monchique in the Serra de Monchique mountains (~1 hour from Lagos). Explore the village, visit the thermal spa town of Caldas de Monchique, and enjoy the lush green mountain scenery — a striking contrast to the coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a quiet evening with dinner at Restaurante Laranjeira — an intimate, upscale Lagos restaurant known for its creative Portuguese cuisine, excellent wine cellar, and warm, personal service.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh fruit, yogurt, local pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch in Silves at Café Inglês — a charming restaurant set in the castle gardens, serving regional Algarvian dishes with local wines
meals.dinner: Restaurante Laranjeira, Lagos — creative tasting menu featuring seasonal Algarvian ingredients with a curated wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private driver for this full-day excursion. The mountain roads to Monchique are winding — a driver allows you to relax and enjoy the scenery. September is ideal for mountain visits as temperatures are cooler than the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — enjoy the hotel, take a swim, or explore the Lagos marina area. Mid-morning, join a private stand-up paddleboard (SUP) or kayak session along the Lagos coastline for a gentle active experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic drive (~1.5 hours) east to the Ria Formosa Natural Park near Faro — a stunning coastal lagoon system. Join a private boat tour through the lagoon, visiting barrier islands, flamingo habitats, and pristine sandbar beaches accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Faro before returning to Lagos — visit Faro's charming old town (Cidade Velha) for a pre-dinner stroll, then enjoy dinner at Restaurante Cidade Velha — an elegant restaurant within the historic walled city, renowned for its refined Portuguese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on one of the Ria Formosa barrier islands — many boat tours include a stop at a local seafood shack serving oysters, clams, and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Restaurante Cidade Velha, Faro — duck rice, grilled sea bass, and local Alentejo wines in a historic setting

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transport to Faro and back (~1.5 hours each way). Book the Ria Formosa private boat tour in advance. The lagoon is a UNESCO-protected area — a truly special natural experience.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, enjoy a full morning at Praia Dona Ana again — the beach is typically quieter mid-week in late September. Rent a premium sun lounger, swim, and explore the sea caves at low tide on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel and freshen up. Spend the afternoon on a private guided food and market tour of Lagos — visit local producers, taste regional specialties including carob products, fig sweets, local olive oils, and artisan preserves with a culinary guide.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a premium sunset cocktail cruise from Lagos Marina — a 2-hour private sailing experience along the golden cliffs at dusk, with Champagne, canapés, and a professional skipper. One of the most romantic experiences the Algarve offers.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh pastries, smoked salmon, eggs, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the beach — arrange through the hotel with premium sandwiches, salads, local cheeses, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Muralha, Lagos — set within the historic city walls, offering refined Portuguese cuisine and an excellent wine list in a romantic setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset cocktail cruise at least 2 days in advance — private charters are popular in September. The food tour can be arranged through the hotel concierge or a local culinary experience company.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning drive (~1 hour) to the stunning Sagres Peninsula — the wild, windswept southwestern tip of Portugal. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress), walk the dramatic clifftops, and explore the legendary Escola de Sagres where Henry the Navigator planned his voyages of discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Praia do Beliche and Praia de Sagres — wild, unspoiled Atlantic beaches with powerful surf and dramatic scenery. Watch surfers tackle the waves or simply enjoy the raw, elemental beauty of this remote coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a final evening in the western Algarve. Celebrate with a special dinner at Vila Joya (Michelin 2-star, Albufeira, ~1 hour east) — one of Portugal's finest restaurants, offering an extraordinary tasting menu in a clifftop setting above the sea.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with fresh orange juice and local pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Bossa Nova, Sagres — a relaxed, quality seafood restaurant in Sagres village with fresh catches and local wines
meals.dinner: Vila Joya, Albufeira — 2-Michelin-star tasting menu with full wine pairing (reservation essential, book weeks in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Vila Joya is one of Portugal's most celebrated restaurants — reservations must be made well in advance. Arrange a private driver for the evening so you can fully enjoy the wine pairing. The drive from Lagos to Vila Joya is approximately 1 hour.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final full morning — enjoy an extended hotel breakfast and take a slow, nostalgic walk through Lagos old town. Visit any shops or galleries you may have missed, pick up premium local souvenirs (artisan ceramics, local wines, carob liqueur, fleur de sel).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Meia Praia for one last long beach session — swim, sunbathe, and soak in the vast Atlantic views. Alternatively, book a final spa treatment or massage at a luxury wellness center for total relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the finest table in Lagos — return to Dom Sebastião or try Restaurante Atlântico at the Cascade Wellness Resort (~15 min from Lagos) for a spectacular clifftop fine-dining farewell with panoramic ocean views and an exceptional wine list.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — order everything you loved during the trip one last time
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch at Meia Praia — fresh grilled fish, salads, and a final glass of chilled Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Restaurante Atlântico, Cascade Wellness Resort — premium tasting menu with Algarve and Alentejo wine pairing, ocean views at sunset

day_by_day.notes: Pack and prepare luggage this evening for the following day's departure. Confirm private airport transfer for Day 13. Leave time to enjoy the hotel one last time — perhaps a final nightcap on the terrace under the stars.

day_by_day.morning: Final hotel breakfast at leisure. Check out of Boutique Taghostel — take your time and enjoy the last moments in Lagos. Take a final short walk to the Lagos waterfront or marina for a last look at the Algarve coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, either head directly to Faro Airport via pre-arranged private luxury transfer (~55 min), or if time allows, stop at a café in Lagos for a final bica (espresso) and pastel de nata before departing.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of golden beaches, world-class wines, dramatic sea caves, Michelin-starred dining, and the timeless beauty of Portugal's Algarve coast.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — fresh pastries, fruit, cheese, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a café en route if time permits
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private transfer to Faro Airport the evening before. Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Faro. Consider purchasing local wines, ceramics, or artisan products as final souvenirs before leaving Lagos.
